close_reason: Decision: option (i) pkix-aia. New workspace crate + pkix-aia-http adapter. Matches existing trust-domain seam pattern. Implementation children unblocked.
description:
## Decision

Pick where the `AiaFetcher` trait + `NoAiaFetcher` default + `AiaError` type live. Blocks PKIX-zkjb.2 (AiaError) and PKIX-zkjb.3 (trait def).

## Options

### (i) pkix-aia (new workspace crate)

Matches the existing trust-domain seam pattern: SignatureVerifier in pkix-path, RevocationChecker in pkix-revocation, AiaFetcher in pkix-aia. Each thematic concern gets its own crate.

- Pros: consistent naming, clean separation, std-vs-no_std boundary explicit, sibling adapter crate `pkix-aia-http` mirrors `pkix-revocation-http`.
- Cons: adds a workspace member. The core crate is small (one trait, one default impl, one error type, maybe a helper to extract AIA URIs from a cert — though that already exists in pkix-revocation-http).

### (ii) pkix-chain

Hosts the trait alongside its existing re-exports of SignatureVerifier and RevocationChecker. Centralizes the trust-domain seam in one place.

- Pros: cohesion — pkix-chain is the orchestrator and owns the seam shape. Fewer crates. Easier for callers to discover all three callbacks together.
- Cons: breaks the existing pattern. SignatureVerifier and RevocationChecker live in their thematic crates; pkix-chain only re-exports. Moving the trait definition itself there is inconsistent.

### (iii) pkix-revocation

Reuses the existing crate, which already has the std-only HTTP adapter pattern (pkix-revocation-http) and the helper `extract_aia_http_urls`.

- Pros: minimal crate churn. AIA fetching reuses pkix-revocation-http directly. The existing helper to extract AIA URIs is right there.
- Cons: semantic misfit. AIA is "online intermediate retrieval"; revocation is "is this cert revoked." Putting AiaFetcher in pkix-revocation conflates two RFC 5280 concerns. Bad signposting for callers.

## Recommendation

**Option (i): pkix-aia.** Matches existing pattern, cleanest separation of concerns, std-vs-no_std boundary explicit. Cost: one new workspace crate (small). Benefit: consistent naming and structure across the trust-domain seam.

(ii) is defensible if you want to minimize crate count. (iii) is a semantic misfit and probably wrong.

## Implementation consequences after decision

- (i): file new `pkix-aia` core crate (no_std-friendly, sync) + `pkix-aia-http` adapter crate. The AIA-URI helper migrates from pkix-revocation-http to pkix-aia (or stays in pkix-revocation-http with re-export — minor).
- (ii): trait definition lives in pkix-chain alongside `verify_chain`. NoAiaFetcher in pkix-chain. HTTP adapter still needs its own std-only crate (pkix-aia-http or fold into pkix-chain-http if that ever exists).
- (iii): trait in pkix-revocation. HttpFetcher impl in pkix-revocation-http. The helper is already there. Naming becomes awkward (`pkix_revocation::AiaFetcher` reads oddly).

## Out of scope for this decision

- HTTP adapter crate name (will follow from the choice).
- Default-impl behavior (already locked: NoAiaFetcher returns AiaError::FetchingDisabled).
- Batch fetch method shape (already locked: batch_fetch with default-impl loop).
notes:
[2026-05-13 decision: option (i) pkix-aia]

Mark picked (i): new `pkix-aia` core workspace crate (no_std-friendly, sync), with `pkix-aia-http` as the std-only adapter crate for HTTP fetching.

Reasoning (per bead recommendation):
- Matches existing trust-domain seam pattern (SignatureVerifier in pkix-path, RevocationChecker in pkix-revocation)
- Cleanest separation of concerns; std-vs-no_std boundary explicit
- Sibling adapter crate `pkix-aia-http` mirrors `pkix-revocation-http` naming

Rejected:
- (ii) pkix-chain: would break the thematic-per-crate pattern
- (iii) pkix-revocation: semantic misfit — AIA is intermediate retrieval, not revocation status

## Implementation consequences locked in

- Two new workspace crates: `pkix-aia` (core, no_std-friendly, sync) and `pkix-aia-http` (std-only adapter)
- `AiaFetcher` trait, `NoAiaFetcher` default impl, and `AiaError` type all live in `pkix-aia`
- The AIA-URI extraction helper `extract_aia_http_urls` currently in `pkix-revocation-http` should migrate to `pkix-aia` (or stay in pkix-revocation-http with a re-export from pkix-aia — implementation detail, defer to .5/.6 work)
- pkix-chain re-exports AiaFetcher alongside its existing re-exports of SignatureVerifier and RevocationChecker (so callers see the full trust-domain seam from pkix-chain)
- `pkix-aia-http::HttpFetcher` is the std-only sync impl; async variant via reqwest::blocking::Client or ureq

human label removed; bead closes as decided.
title: Decide AiaFetcher trait location: pkix-aia (new crate) vs pkix-chain vs pkix-revocation
